problem: Existing embodied agents and LLM-agent frameworks (Reflexion, Sophia, Evolving Agents) either depend on externally scripted goals and fixed rewards or are disembodied and ignore physical constraints such as energy. Social-robot personality models treat personality as a static design parameter rather than as a source of goals. None of them can generate their own objectives and keep operating for long periods on a real robot without task specifications.
motivation: Long-term deployments such as eldercare companions or exploration rovers need agents that decide for themselves what to do, when, and how to trade off opportunity against risk and resources, because continuous human supervision is impractical. The authors draw on biology, where stable personality traits act like genotypic biases that organize behavior over a lifetime. They propose personality as the intrinsic organizing principle for autonomous goal generation.
key_idea: A natural-language personality description conditions a cloud LLM (Sys3) that generates ultimate and daily goals plus incremental intrinsic-reward adjustments from daily episodic-memory reflection; a BERT policy distilled from LLM-MCTS (Sys2) picks actions on-device; a robot skill layer (Sys1) executes actions, including elevator and staircase multi-floor navigation, and logs episodic memories.
insight: Splitting slow, high-quality reflection from fast per-step decisions is what makes persistent operation feasible. In the architecture comparison (Table IV), an all-cloud Qwen3-235B agent matches PEPA's 24 h Day-3 survival but needs 320.6 cloud calls/day at 25.64 s latency. An all-edge Qwen2.5-1.5B agent is real-time (3.54 s) but survives only 2.85 h by Day 3 because it cannot reflect effectively. PEPA uses 1 cloud call/day and 0.15 s on-device latency. Memory-driven daily reflection turns universal Day-1 battery-depletion failures into full 24 h survival on Day 3 (72–100% battery remaining) while sharpening trait-consistent behavior, e.g. Lazy rest share rising from 14.5% to 49.8%. On the navigation side, a height-aligned local costmap is decisive for stairs: 10/10 real trials versus 0/10 for fixed-height slicing.
method: Problem formulation: a POMDP with composite reward R_total = R_intrinsic + R_extrinsic, where R_intrinsic = Sys3(personality, memory, capability description, state); an open-ended-evolution criterion (Adams et al.) requires non-repeating goal-conditioned trajectories.

Sys3 (personality & goal generation): Qwen3-235B on the cloud takes a three-sentence natural-language personality prompt (Big Five-inspired; the trait coordinates themselves are not given to the model), a self-model (battery, emotional valence, recent interactions, available APIs and their preconditions) and retrieved memories. It outputs an ultimate goal plus daily goals and, once per day, reflects over episodic memory to emit incremental adjustments to the reward function (e.g. extra rest weight, penalty for low-battery exploration).

Sys2 (decision & reasoning): LLM-based MCTS with UCT selection, the LLM serving as policy prior, value estimator and world model, generates state-action pairs offline. A lightweight dual-head BERT is distilled from these pairs: a multi-label intent head on [CLS] predicts actions and a BIO slot-filling head extracts location/method arguments. It runs in real time on a Jetson Orin NX.

Sys1 (perception/execution/memory): Livox Mid-360 LiDAR multi-floor SLAM (Open3D_loc/FAST-LIO), a wrist RealSense D405 with YOLO for elevator buttons and lanterns plus depth projection, proprioception, a global planner with DWA local planner on prebuilt maps, and 19 discrete high-level actions (idle, 8 locomotion primitives, 8 emotional expressions, move_to(location, method)). Each action writes a structured episodic record (command, pre/post state, outcome, energy/time, context) stored hierarchically at minute/hour, daily and long-term scales.

Elevator skill: a four-phase finite state machine (call, wait, enter and select floor, exit with relocalization), with coarse global navigation, fine alignment and visual-servoing button presses using a 6-DOF Piper arm.
Staircase skill: builds on PCT-planner and adds a height-aligned costmap that uses Δz = z(p) − z(r) relative to the nearest global-path waypoint, so the DWA controller works on inclines.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-235B (frozen, cloud, prompt-based Sys3) + dual-head BERT distilled from LLM-MCTS (Sys2, on-device); classical SLAM/global planner/DWA for low-level navigation
setting.training_data: Sys2 BERT distilled from LLM-MCTS state-action pairs collected in a rule-based sandbox simulator (scale not reported); YOLO trained for elevator buttons/lanterns/light states; Sys3 is training-free (prompting + reflection)
setting.observation: Livox Mid-360 LiDAR + wrist RealSense D405 RGB-D + proprioception (battery, joint temperature, locomotion mode), abstracted into semantic state for Sys2/Sys3
setting.action_space: 19 discrete high-level actions (idle, 8 locomotion primitives, 8 emotional expressions, move_to(location, method)); executed via global planner + DWA velocity commands, elevator FSM, stair traversal
setting.simulator: hand-crafted rule-based sandbox simulator (battery/temperature/charging calibrated from hardware) for personality experiments; real world for deployment
setting.privileged: prebuilt multi-floor maps and named locations for move_to; sandbox experiments use an abstract simulated state (battery, mood, location)

numbers.backbone: Qwen3-235B (Sys3, cloud) + distilled dual-head BERT (Sys2, on-device)
numbers.extra: custom rule-based sandbox; averaged over five personality prototypes; Sys3 invoked once per day

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is used. The persistent-autonomy results come from a custom sandbox simulator, and several results appear only in figures: Fig. 4 action-category trends and Fig. 5 survival time, plus text mentions of Day-3 remaining battery of 72%–100% and Lazy rest share of 14.5%→49.8%. The action-preference results (Table III) are percentages from 10 trials per personality and scenario. Elevator navigation is shown qualitatively, with no success-rate table.
results: In a three-day sandbox loop, all five personalities fail from battery depletion on Day 1. After daily memory-driven reflection, all of them survive the full 24 h on Day 3 with 72–100% battery left, and their action distributions become more trait-consistent. The strongest baseline, a single cloud LLM (all-cloud Qwen3-235B), matches the 24 h survival but needs 320.6 calls/day at 25.64 s latency, versus PEPA's 1 call/day and 0.15 s. The all-edge Qwen2.5-1.5B baseline reaches only 2.85 h. On the real Go2-W robot, the height-aligned costmap achieves 10/10 stair traversals versus 0/10 for fixed-height slicing, and the system demonstrates elevator-based multi-floor operation and autonomous charging.
limitations: Sys1 has a fixed, finite action repertoire (19 actions), which limits the behavioral novelty that Sys3's goal refinement can express (stated by the authors).

Personality and self-evolution experiments run only in a hand-crafted rule-based sandbox over 3 days with 5 prototypes and 10 trials per condition, with no quantitative personality-alignment metric. Real-world evidence is mostly qualitative apart from 10 stair trials.

Real-world navigation relies on prebuilt maps and predefined named locations. No standard navigation benchmark is used, and the LLM-MCTS/distillation details (data scale, which LLM, accuracy) are sparse.
